jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Senior Regulatory Toxicologist (Toxicologist 3)
within the Hazardous Waste and Toxics Reduction Program (HWTR).

Location:

Headquarters Office in Lacey, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
A minimum of two days per month is required in the office.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by November 18, 2026.
Applications submitted after the date above may be reviewed only if additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

This Senior Regulatory Toxicologist position offers a key opportunity to shape Washington’s toxics-reduction policies and advance statewide protections for human health and the environment. In this role, you will serve as the program’s senior regulatory subject matter expert, providing authoritative toxicological leadership for identifying, evaluating, and reducing threats from high-priority chemicals used in commerce. You will guide the scientific direction of the Safer Products for Washington initiative, lead complex hazard evaluations, and translate emerging toxicological research into actionable policy recommendations that support Ecology’s mission.

You will also direct the toxicology work of staff within the Toxics Awareness and Action Section and collaborate with scientific partners at the Washington Department of Health. Working closely with program leadership, you will assess the implications of emerging science, regulatory developments, and legislative proposals; communicate complex findings to technical and non-technical audiences; and help build consensus on major policy and regulatory decisions. Your work will influence statewide toxics-reduction strategies, support rulemaking and program planning, and ensure that Ecology’s actions are grounded in rigorous scientific analysis and consistent with best available science.

What You Will Do

Provide senior-level toxicological expertise and policy guidance for Ecology’s toxics-reduction initiatives, including the identification and evaluation of priority chemicals that pose the highest potential impacts to human health and the environment.
Lead the scientific framework for Safer Products for Washington by developing hazard criteria, evaluating toxicological and exposure data, and directing research to inform statewide chemical prioritization and recommended regulatory actions.
Assign, guide, and review the technical work of toxicologists within Ecology and the Washington Department of Health, ensuring scientific quality, consistency, and clarity across assessments and policy support.
Conduct and oversee toxicological assessments that identify major sources of exposure in consumer products, and provide expert recommendations for regulatory options, reporting requirements, or restrictions under Chapter 70.365 RCW.
Represent Ecology as a senior scientific expert in briefings, legislative hearings, interagency meetings, national workgroups, and public forums, communicating complex toxicological findings in clear, accessible terms.
Analyze state and federal regulatory developments, scientific literature, and emerging research to assess implications for Washington’s toxics-reduction strategy and support program decisions, bill analysis, and testimony preparation.
Develop and refine methodologies for evaluating chemical hazards and exposures, assess scientific rigor and uncertainty in studies, and adapt approaches used by federal agencies or other jurisdictions for application in Washington.
Provide toxicology support for Chemical Action Plans, product testing studies, QAPP development, regulatory implementation, and compliance activities.
Contribute to program planning and policy development by advising the Program Manager and Management Team on scientific considerations, resource needs, and long-term strategies to reduce toxic threats statewide.
Prepare and deliver presentations, workshops, and webinars; author or co-author scientific publications; and ensure that Ecology’s scientific work is broadly accessible and accurately communicated to varied audiences.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Ten (10) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which includes the following:

Toxicology & Public Health Expertise — Ability to apply toxicology and public health knowledge to assess human and ecological health impacts resulting from exposure to priority chemicals and chemical classes, including impacts on sensitive populations and sensitive species.
Regulatory and Policy Analysis Skill in reviewing and interpreting state and federal environmental laws, rules, and scientific policy documents to inform program decisions and develop recommended regulatory actions.
Science Policy Support — Ability to identify ecological and human health risk implications of proposed legislation and regulatory developments, and to support bill analysis, testimony preparation, and agency toxics-reduction strategy.
Science Communication Ability to translate complex toxicological and scientific information into clear, accessible language for diverse technical and non-technical audiences, including agency leadership and legislators.
Technical Leadership and Work Direction Experience leading and coordinating scientific work, assigning and reviewing technical tasks, and providing expert guidance and direction to cross-disciplinary staff and interagency partners.
Hazard & Risk Framework Development — Ability to research, develop, and apply a hazard- and exposure-based framework for identifying and prioritizing chemicals of concern, distinct from a risk-assessment approach.
Research and Scientific Method Application Demonstrated competency in designing, conducting, or reviewing scientific research, evaluating uncertainties, and applying sound methodology to support hazard, exposure, or risk analyses. Ability to assess the scientific rigor, quality, uncertainty and applicability of toxicological and exposure studies to problems being addressed in Washington.
Interested Parties & Interagency Engagement — Ability to represent the program to the Legislature, other state and federal agencies, Tribes, and the public, including serving as agency liaison/spokesperson and building consensus among parties with diverse interests.

Education
: Involving a major study in toxicology, reproductive and developmental biology, or in another health or ecological related science with a major emphasis in toxicology.

Examples Of How To Qualify

10 years of experience.
9 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
8 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
7 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
6 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
4 years of experience AND a Master’s degree or above.

Desired Qualifications

Diplomat of the American Board of Toxicology (DABT) or similar certification – either existing or willingness to obtain certification.
Experience in one or more of the following disciplines: chemical hazard assessments, alternatives assessments, chemical risk evaluations, exposure assessments, health impact assessments, or green chemistry.
Experience with toxicology tools, models, and chemical data base systems (e.g. ToxCast).
Awareness or involvement with toxicology professional organizations such as the Society of Toxicology (SOT), Society of Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry (SETAC) and other professional networks.

Supplemental Information

system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov .

Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

Diversity:
We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.

Equity:
We champion equity, recognizing that each of us need different things to thrive.

Inclusion:
We intentionally create and hold space so that we all have meaningful opportunities to participate and contribute to Ecology’s work.

Respect:
We treat each other with respect and dignity, acknowledging the inherent worth of our diverse perspectives and lived experiences, even in times of uncertainty and disagreement.

We believe that DEIRis both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Position Summary
We are seeking an experienced Senior Health & Safety Manager to lead all environmental, health, and safety (EHS) programs for a large-scale semiconductor manufacturing facility. This individual will be responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving site-wide safety systems that support advanced manufacturing, cleanroom operations, chemical management, construction activities, and high-hazard process environments.
The ideal candidate will possess deep expertise in semiconductor manufacturing safety, OSHA compliance, contractor safety management, process safety, industrial hygiene, and emergency preparedness. This leader will partner closely with operations, facilities, engineering, construction, and executive leadership teams to foster a proactive safety culture and ensure regulatory compliance while supporting critical production objectives.
Key Responsibilities
Safety Leadership & Strategy
Lead the site's EHS strategy and drive continuous improvement initiatives across all manufacturing, facilities, and support operations.
Establish and maintain a world-class safety culture focused on risk prevention, accountability, and employee engagement.
Serve as the primary advisor to site leadership on health, safety, and regulatory matters.
Develop annual EHS objectives, metrics, and performance improvement plans.

Regulatory Compliance
Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations including:
OSHA
EPA
NFPA
ANSI
SEMI Standards
State environmental agencies
Manage regulatory inspections, audits, and agency interactions.
Develop and maintain site safety policies, procedures, permits, and compliance documentation.
Monitor regulatory changes and implement program updates as required.

Semiconductor Manufacturing & Process Safety
Support high-volume semiconductor manufacturing operations including cleanrooms, wafer fabrication, and advanced processing equipment.
Lead Process Hazard Analyses (PHA), Job Hazard Analyses (JHA), and risk assessments.
Oversee safety programs involving:
Hazardous chemicals
Toxic gas systems
Specialty gases
Wet process chemicals
Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP)
Process exhaust systems
High-voltage electrical systems
Automated material handling systems
Evaluate and mitigate operational risks associated with manufacturing equipment and facilities systems.

Industrial Hygiene & Occupational Health
Manage industrial hygiene monitoring programs.
Oversee exposure assessments related to:
Chemical hazards
Airborne contaminants
Noise
Ergonomics
Radiation sources where applicable
Develop and maintain respiratory protection, hearing conservation, and medical surveillance programs.
Coordinate occupational health initiatives and employee wellness programs.

Contractor & Construction Safety
Lead contractor safety management programs supporting construction, expansion, retrofit, and maintenance projects.
Conduct contractor onboarding, audits, and performance evaluations.
Ensure compliance during:
New tool installations
Facility shutdowns
Capital projects
Utility upgrades
Cleanroom construction efforts
Partner with project teams to integrate safety requirements into project execution plans.

Incident Investigation & Risk Management
Lead investigations of incidents, near misses, and high-potential events.
Conduct root cause analyses and implement corrective actions.
Track leading and lagging indicators to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.
Develop strategies to reduce Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR) and improve overall safety performance.

Description/Job Summary

POSITION DESCRIPTION

HGL is seeking a Risk Assessor II to support environmental projects, including hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste; PFAS; mining; and military munitions response program projects nationwide. The Risk Assessor II will prepare human health risk assessments and/or ecological risk assessments in accordance with CERCLA, RCRA, and applicable state guidance, with support from HGL’s risk assessment team, including senior- and principal-level staff. The ideal candidate can lead both human health and ecological risk assessments; candidates with strong experience in either discipline will also be considered. This role is well suited for a self-directed individual who enjoys integrating complex environmental data, technical analysis, and regulatory requirements to support sound project and remedial decisions. HGL is seeking to fill one hybrid position based out of our Denver office in Lakewood, CO.

Responsibilities/Duties

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Manage and analyze large environmental datasets.
Prepare tables, figures, and other data exhibits.
Author risk assessments, risk assessment work plans, and other technical deliverables.
Review and interpret environmental and toxicological studies and reports.
Support remedial strategy design, including development of risk-based cleanup levels.
Conduct statistical analyses, including statistical comparisons of background data to site data.
Serve as the project risk assessor in project meetings and technical discussions with clients, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders.
Lead and provide technical direction to junior-level staff.

Minimum Requirements

WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

Bachelor’s degree in toxicology, environmental science, public health, engineering, or a related health or environmental science discipline.
At least 6 years of work experience in an environmental consulting or regulatory environment on DoD or EPA projects, with a focus on site investigation and human health or ecological risk assessment; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience implementing EPA’s Risk Assessment Guidance for Superfund and/or EPA’s Ecological Risk Assessment Guidance for Superfund.
Working knowledge of relevant federal regulations, especially CERCLA and RCRA, and the ability to integrate federal requirements with varying state regulations.
Ability to present technical information effectively to scientific, regulatory, and public audiences.
Ability to succeed in a fast-paced consulting environment, manage multiple project assignments, meet strict deadlines, travel to client facilities as needed, and work independently as a self-starter.
Demonstrated ability to learn and adopt new technologies and digital tools to improve project delivery and operational efficiency.

Desired Qualifications

Advanced degree (MS, MPH, or PhD) in toxicology, environmental science, public health, engineering, or a related health or environmental science discipline.
Experience completing statistical comparisons of site data to background data and geochemical evaluations to distinguish site-related contaminants from background constituents.
Experience in technical areas beyond risk assessment—such as contaminant fate and transport, analytical chemistry, characterization of the nature and extent of contamination, or development of remediation strategies—to support integration across project teams.
Experience designing and leading baseline ecological risk assessments that include collection of site-specific data, such as biota tissue, toxicity testing, bioaccumulation studies, or habitat and/or species surveys.
Experience in blood lead modeling to support human health risk assessments.
Familiarity with environmental databases, primarily LOCUS, and statistical software.
Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

we’re committed to helping you thrive while you help our city flourish. Be part of a team that’s committed to service, innovation, and community.

Under minimum to no supervision, performs complex environmental work. Inspects public and private facilities, indoor and outdoor sites, and investigates incidents to determine compliance with environmental laws and regulations. Overview

The Environmental Specialist III conducts inspections and investigations of public and private sites to ensure compliance with environmental laws and standards. Responds to review requests, prepares detailed reports, supports audits through site visits and documents reviews, and collects and analyzes environmental samples. The role also includes managing hazardous waste disposal, assisting with document control, and supporting interdepartmental investigations and water quality programs.

Experience in sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, including aseptic processing, sterility assurance, contamination control, injectable products, IV solutions, and/or terminal sterilization.

Strong program and portfolio management discipline, including management of scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, resources, and change.

Ability to travel as needed to support regulatory inspections, remediation activities, and enterprise governance.

Formal certification in project or program management, Lean Six Sigma, quality management, or change management.
Experience leading remediation in a multi-building pharmaceutical operation or a complex sterile-manufacturing network.

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Senior Regulatory Toxicologist (Toxicologist 3)

Duties

This Senior Regulatory Toxicologist position offers a key opportunity to shape Washington’s toxics-reduction policies and advance statewide protections for human health and the environment. In this role, you will serve as the program’s senior regulatory subject matter expert, providing authoritative toxicological leadership for identifying, evaluating, and reducing threats from high-priority chemicals used in commerce. You will guide the scientific direction of the Safer Products for Washington initiative, lead complex hazard evaluations, and translate emerging toxicological research into actionable policy recommendations that support Ecology’s mission.

You will also direct the toxicology work of staff within the Toxics Awareness and Action Section and collaborate with scientific partners at the Washington Department of Health. Working closely with program leadership, you will assess the implications of emerging science, regulatory developments, and legislative proposals; communicate complex findings to technical and non-technical audiences; and help build consensus on major policy and regulatory decisions. Your work will influence statewide toxics-reduction strategies, support rulemaking and program planning, and ensure that Ecology’s actions are grounded in rigorous scientific analysis and consistent with best available science.

What You Will Do

Provide senior-level toxicological expertise and policy guidance for Ecology’s toxics-reduction initiatives, including the identification and evaluation of priority chemicals that pose the highest potential impacts to human health and the environment.
Lead the scientific framework for Safer Products for Washington by developing hazard criteria, evaluating toxicological and exposure data, and directing research to inform statewide chemical prioritization and recommended regulatory actions.
Assign, guide, and review the technical work of toxicologists within Ecology and the Washington Department of Health, ensuring scientific quality, consistency, and clarity across assessments and policy support.
Conduct and oversee toxicological assessments that identify major sources of exposure in consumer products, and provide expert recommendations for regulatory options, reporting requirements, or restrictions under Chapter 70.365 RCW.
Represent Ecology as a senior scientific expert in briefings, legislative hearings, interagency meetings, national workgroups, and public forums, communicating complex toxicological findings in clear, accessible terms.
Analyze state and federal regulatory developments, scientific literature, and emerging research to assess implications for Washington’s toxics-reduction strategy and support program decisions, bill analysis, and testimony preparation.

Contribute to program planning and policy development by advising the Program Manager and Management Team on scientific considerations, resource needs, and long-term strategies to reduce toxic threats statewide.
Prepare and deliver presentations, workshops, and webinars; author or co-author scientific publications; and ensure that Ecology’s scientific work is broadly accessible and accurately communicated to varied audiences.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Ten (10) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which includes the following:

Toxicology & Public Health Expertise — Ability to apply toxicology and public health knowledge to assess human and ecological health impacts resulting from exposure to priority chemicals and chemical classes, including impacts on sensitive populations and sensitive species.
Regulatory and Policy Analysis Skill in reviewing and interpreting state and federal environmental laws, rules, and scientific policy documents to inform program decisions and develop recommended regulatory actions.
Science Policy Support — Ability to identify ecological and human health risk implications of proposed legislation and regulatory developments, and to support bill analysis, testimony preparation, and agency toxics-reduction strategy.
Science Communication Ability to translate complex toxicological and scientific information into clear, accessible language for diverse technical and non-technical audiences, including agency leadership and legislators.

Hazard & Risk Framework Development — Ability to research, develop, and apply a hazard- and exposure-based framework for identifying and prioritizing chemicals of concern, distinct from a risk-assessment approach.
Research and Scientific Method Application Demonstrated competency in designing, conducting, or reviewing scientific research, evaluating uncertainties, and applying sound methodology to support hazard, exposure, or risk analyses. Ability to assess the scientific rigor, quality, uncertainty and applicability of toxicological and exposure studies to problems being addressed in Washington.
Interested Parties & Interagency Engagement — Ability to represent the program to the Legislature, other state and federal agencies, Tribes, and the public, including serving as agency liaison/spokesperson and building consensus among parties with diverse interests.

Job Title:
Risk Assessor II

Location:
Lakewood, CO

Description/Job Summary

POSITION DESCRIPTION

HGL is seeking a Risk Assessor II to support environmental projects, including hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste; PFAS; mining; and military munitions response program projects nationwide. The Risk Assessor II will prepare human health risk assessments and/or ecological risk assessments in accordance with CERCLA, RCRA, and applicable state guidance, with support from HGL’s risk assessment team, including senior- and principal-level staff. The ideal candidate can lead both human health and ecological risk assessments; candidates with strong experience in either discipline will also be considered. This role is well suited for a self-directed individual who enjoys integrating complex environmental data, technical analysis, and regulatory requirements to support sound project and remedial decisions. HGL is seeking to fill one hybrid position based out of our Denver office in Lakewood, CO.

Responsibilities/Duties

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Manage and analyze large environmental datasets.
Prepare tables, figures, and other data exhibits.
Author risk assessments, risk assessment work plans, and other technical deliverables.
Review and interpret environmental and toxicological studies and reports.
Support remedial strategy design, including development of risk-based cleanup levels.
Conduct statistical analyses, including statistical comparisons of background data to site data.
Serve as the project risk assessor in project meetings and technical discussions with clients, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders.
Lead and provide technical direction to junior-level staff.

Minimum Requirements

WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

Bachelor’s degree in toxicology, environmental science, public health, engineering, or a related health or environmental science discipline.
At least 6 years of work experience in an environmental consulting or regulatory environment on DoD or EPA projects, with a focus on site investigation and human health or ecological risk assessment; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience implementing EPA’s Risk Assessment Guidance for Superfund and/or EPA’s Ecological Risk Assessment Guidance for Superfund.
Working knowledge of relevant federal regulations, especially CERCLA and RCRA, and the ability to integrate federal requirements with varying state regulations.
Ability to present technical information effectively to scientific, regulatory, and public audiences.
Ability to succeed in a fast-paced consulting environment, manage multiple project assignments, meet strict deadlines, travel to client facilities as needed, and work independently as a self-starter.
Demonstrated ability to learn and adopt new technologies and digital tools to improve project delivery and operational efficiency.

Desired Qualifications

WHAT YOU NEED TO STAND OUT – Preferred, not required

Advanced degree (MS, MPH, or PhD) in toxicology, environmental science, public health, engineering, or a related health or environmental science discipline.
Experience completing statistical comparisons of site data to background data and geochemical evaluations to distinguish site-related contaminants from background constituents.
Experience in technical areas beyond risk assessment—such as contaminant fate and transport, analytical chemistry, characterization of the nature and extent of contamination, or development of remediation strategies—to support integration across project teams.
Experience designing and leading baseline ecological risk assessments that include collection of site-specific data, such as biota tissue, toxicity testing, bioaccumulation studies, or habitat and/or species surveys.
Experience in blood lead modeling to support human health risk assessments.
Familiarity with environmental databases, primarily LOCUS, and statistical software.
Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

Prolonged sitting up to 70% of the time.
Viewing computer screen for extended periods.
Analyzing and synthesizing data.
Managing competing deadlines and shifting priorities.

Office work environment.

Minimal but as needed to client facilities; percentage varies by project assignment.

Dallas is Growing. Grow With Us.

we’re committed to helping you thrive while you help our city flourish. Be part of a team that’s committed to service, innovation, and community.

Job Summary

Under minimum to no supervision, performs complex environmental work. Inspects public and private facilities, indoor and outdoor sites, and investigates incidents to determine compliance with environmental laws and regulations. Works independently and is responsible for making decisions requiring technical discretion, sound judgement, and specialized knowledge.

Overview

Job Description

The Environmental Specialist III conducts inspections and investigations of public and private sites to ensure compliance with environmental laws and standards. Responds to review requests, prepares detailed reports, supports audits through site visits and documents reviews, and collects and analyzes environmental samples. The role also includes managing hazardous waste disposal, assisting with document control, and supporting interdepartmental investigations and water quality programs.

Essential Functions

1 Travels through the City of Dallas to inspect and evaluate various public and private facilities utilizing ISO standards; performs complex environmental evaluations, inspections, and reviews city services and utilities; investigates complaints, and files compliance reports for environmental agencies. Conducts water quality monitoring and sampling, collects grab samples, preserves sample integrity, records field results, and prepares samples for laboratory analysis to meet program requirements.

2 Oversees, monitors, and provides experience-based skill for cleaning spills and other potentially hazardous situations affecting the MS4; ensures spills are cleaned appropriately, investigates causes of incidents to determine preventability, and ensures incident reports are filed accordingly.

3 Inspects public and private sites and indoor/outdoor facilities for environmental compliance; reviews waste storage areas, workplace chemical lists, water facilities, SCBA equipment, stormwater management tactics, permits, and other water activities; observes and identifies issues, mitigates and follows through the resolution of the identified issues.

4 Reviews and files extensive data-driven reports on inspections, service requests and spill response activities; documents areas of non-compliance, produces preventable reports, makes recommendations on various incidents; ensures all relevant parties are aware of issues and have comprehensive data to make informed decisions; provides follow-ups on compliance investigations. Tracks and maintains inventory of environmental spill response supplies.

5 Applies and enforces environmental policies, rules, regulations, and standards to meet and exceed expectations set by the City of Dallas; provides training and continuous education to other employees to ensure all inspection and compliance activities are completed efficiently.

6 Responds to 24-hour emergency service requests and assists with reports for Environmental Compliance Committee meetings.

7 Reviews permits and regulations regarding various industries and monitors compliance with permitting standards.

8 Maintains compliance with Federal, State and local regulations of a waste storage facility. Supports operations of the generation and disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous waste accumulated by Dallas Fire & Rescue (DFR) and the Stormwater Compliance response team, when necessary. Performs daily operations and required inspections of the Stormwater

Compliance Waste Yard. Conducts deliveries of environmental spill remediation supplies to all DFR fire stations.

9 Performs other work as needed or assigned.

Knowledge and Skills

1 Thorough knowledge of environmental compliance regulations, such as The Clean Water Act (CWA) and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA).

2 Thorough knowledge of environmental procedures and inspection tactics, such as RG-416 Surface Water Monitoring Procedures (Bio Program) and RG-415 TCEQ Surface WQ Monitoring Procedures (Physical & Chemical Monitoring).

3 Expert knowledge of environmental codes, ordinances, and regulations, such as Texas Water Quality Standards.

4 Expertise in performing professional inspections and documenting non-compliance findings.

5 Skill in resolving findings and ensuring issue closure.

6 Skill in developing training materials and educating other specialists and citizens.

7 Ability to provide engagement and follow up to ensure environmental standards are achieved.

8 Advanced skill in communicating effectively both verbally and in writing.

9 Advanced skills in Power BI, GIS, and Excel.

10 Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships.

Experience

Five (5) years of hands-on experience in performing environmental inspections, handling hazardous materials, performing chemical analysis in waste management, spill response or soil/water/air/groundwater sample collection environment.

Licenses and Certifications

Valid driver’s license and good driving record.

A forty (40)-hr HAZWOPER (Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response) certification is required for all spill response divisions.

For Stormwater Neighborhood and Water Reservoir divisions, Registered Environmental Manager (REM) certification is required.

For Stormwater Neighborhood division, a Certified Environmental Storm Water Compliance Professional (CESCP) certification and a Boater Certificate are required.

For Water Quality division, a Boater Certificate and a Class D (or higher) Water license from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) are required.

Education

High School or GED with a study course in sciences, chemistry or biology.

Preferred

OSHA 30-hour Safety Certificate is preferred.
Experience with ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems certified programs is highly preferred.
Experience with maintaining/using Safety Data Sheets (SDS) is preferred.
Experience with inspecting storm sewer/drainage structures (e.g., MS4, outfalls, storm sewer pipe, inlets, wing walls, culverts, junctions, etc.) is preferred.
Experience with Stormwater Permits (Construction General Permit TXR150000 and the Multi Sector General Permit TXR 050000) and Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) are preferred for certain divisions.

Equivalency

An associate degree in chemistry, engineering, environmental or physical sciences field plus three (3) years of the required experience will meet the education and experience requirements.

A bachelor's degree (or higher) in chemistry, environmental or natural sciences field, and one (1) year of the required experience will meet the education and experience requirements.

Other Requirements

Must pass background investigation. No Felony convictions. Cannot currently be on deferred adjudication for any Felony, Class A or Class B Misdemeanor. Availability to work varying shifts including nights, weekends, and holidays. Subject to twenty-four (24) hour call-out. Working conditions include potential exposure to bio-hazardous material(s), hazardous chemicals, inclement weather, and confined spaces.

Salary Range

$25.12 - $28.85

Tetra Tech is seeking a self-motivated, Entry-Level Environmental Scientist / Compliance Specialist to support and expand our landfill and air quality compliance services within the solid waste industry. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong interest in air regulations, landfill gas systems, emissions compliance, and environmental data analysis.

In this role, you will support regulatory compliance programs by analyzing field and operational data, interpreting air quality regulations and permit requirements, preparing compliance reports, and assisting with air permitting and emissions calculations. The primary focus areas include landfill gas monitoring, Surface Emissions Monitoring (SEM), Landfill Gas-to-Energy (LFGTE) Systems, air quality permitting, and compliance with New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Pollutants (NESHAP) regulations applicable to solid waste facilities.

This position is primarily remote, with limited, as-needed travel or occasional site visits. Only those in PST, CST, or MST will be considered.
Candidates must be comfortable working independently with limited supervision while collaborating with project managers, field staff, engineers, and regulatory specialists across geographically dispersed teams.

This position is eligible for our full benefits package including but not limited to Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, Disability, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Health Spending Account (HSA), My Flex Time (MFT - paid time off), 401K, and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The pay range for this position is $55K-$75K annually, based on qualifications, location, and experience. The deadline to apply is 11/12/2026.

Your Role

Review, analyze, and interpret landfill air quality and landfill gas monitoring data, including wellfield data, SEM, and air emissions datasets.
Compare monitoring and operational data against regulatory standards, permit limits, and NSPS/NESHAP criteria to assess compliance.
Prepare environmental compliance reports, including air compliance summaries, monitoring reports, deviation analyses, and regulatory submittals.
Support the development and preparation of air quality permit applications, amendments, and renewals, including emission calculations and regulatory compliance demonstrations.
Collect, manage, track, and organize large datasets related to air emissions, landfill gas, SEM results, and compliance deadlines.
Develop and maintain templates, trackers, and tools to support consistent, accurate, and timely reporting for multiple facilities / landfills.
Coordinate with on-site operations, technicians, and subcontractors to confirm that monitoring, testing, and system performance meet regulatory and permit requirements.
Support Project Managers with deliverables, schedules, and client coordination including procurement of supplies, subcontractor coordination and Work Order development.
Contribute to multidisciplinary teams on engineering, permitting, and environmental projects.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including technical and regulatory writing.
Proficiency in MS Office – specifically Word and Excel.
Ability to work independently in a remote environment, demonstrate initiative, and manage multiple priorities with limited supervision.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively with field staff, engineers, and regulatory agencies.
Valid driver’s license.
Ability and willingness to perform limited travel as required.
Interest and ability in developing technical and leadership skills within the Environmental Compliance field.
